original_question: Determine whether the Sun's thermal energy and luminosity can be explained by neutron capture and beta decay rather than by proton-proton fusion into helium nuclei, whether successive neutron-capture and beta-decay reactions can build heavier isotopes through deuterium, tritium, helium-3, helium-4, and beyond, and whether the resulting thermal power and neutrino production can be tuned to match the observed luminosity and isotopic abundances of the Sun.
target_in_paper: Section 7.5, "Solar dynamics": the Glen Deen bullet-list of "Questions" asking whether neutron capture and beta decay driven by a neutron flux from the solar core, rather than the standard 4p -> 4He + 2e+ + 2nu_e reaction, could supply the Sun's thermal energy/luminosity, build isotopes up the periodic table, and agree with photospheric-abundance and neutrino observations. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/UnfoldingLabyrinth.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper's core alternative-solar-power hypothesis almost verbatim: replacing proton fusion by neutron capture plus beta decay, passing through p+n -> d, d+n -> t, t -> helium-3 by beta decay, helium-3+n -> helium-4, extending to heavier nuclei, and checking both solar power and neutrino output against observations. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/UnfoldingLabyrinth.pdf))
missing_details: The paper explicitly ties the proposal to "the neutron flux from the core"; that source of neutrons should be stated rather than left implicit. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/UnfoldingLabyrinth.pdf))
It asks not only about capture by nuclei, but also whether the remaining neutrons beta-decay and become ionized hydrogen. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/UnfoldingLabyrinth.pdf))
The abundance comparison is specifically to "all the isotopes in the photosphere," not solar abundances in a generic sense. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/UnfoldingLabyrinth.pdf))

The competing standard-model benchmark is stated explicitly as 4p -> 4He + 2e+ + 2nu_e, so a paper-faithful rewrite should name that reaction. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/UnfoldingLabyrinth.pdf))

The buildup of heavier species is described as proceeding "up the periodic table to iron and beyond," which is slightly sharper than simply saying "and beyond." ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/UnfoldingLabyrinth.pdf))

The observational test is quantitative: compute the energy released by each neutron-capture/decay step, tune the neutron flux so the total equals the known solar power, and add up the neutrinos produced by each reaction to compare with observations. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/UnfoldingLabyrinth.pdf))
The paper presents this as a contributed set of open-ended "Questions" in section 7.5, not as a formal theorem or numbered conjecture. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/UnfoldingLabyrinth.pdf))

Nearby background motivates the question by a lower-temperature, condensed-matter solar model in which neutron capture may occur more readily nearer the surface and Population I stars produce heavy elements by neutron capture; this is contextual motivation, not a separate claim to be broadened into the question itself. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/UnfoldingLabyrinth.pdf))
refined_question: Does there exist a solar model with a neutron flux from the core in which some neutrons are captured by nuclei while the rest beta-decay to ionized hydrogen, and in which successive reactions p+n -> d, d+n -> t, t -> ^3He via beta decay, ^3He+n -> ^4He, and analogous neutron-capture/beta-decay steps up the periodic table to iron and beyond produce the isotopes observed in the solar photosphere, such that the total energy released by these reactions accounts for all of the Sun's thermal energy and luminosity and the total neutrino yield agrees with observation, thereby removing the need to take the standard 4p -> ^4He + 2e+ + 2nu_e proton-fusion reaction as the Sun's primary power source? ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/UnfoldingLabyrinth.pdf))
justification: The draft is already very close to the paper: section 7.5 literally asks whether neutron capture and beta decay, rather than proton fusion into helium, could supply all solar thermal energy/luminosity; it then spells out the d/t/^3He/^4He chain, extends the process up the periodic table, and asks for quantitative agreement with solar power, neutrino observations, and photospheric isotopic abundances. The book's preface and chapter-7 framing show that this is part of a broad, partly speculative collection of open questions, so the sharpest stand-alone rewrite should preserve that exact solar-dynamics scope rather than broaden it into a general stellar-nucleosynthesis program. The nearby numbered Conjecture 1 belongs to section 7.4 on Gross-Pitaevskii/Schrodinger equations and is unrelated to the target here. No ambient ring/field, homogeneity, degree, operator, or nilpotency hypotheses are part of the paper's target because this section is an astrophysical question set, not an algebraic theorem. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/UnfoldingLabyrinth.pdf))
